VA's contracting crackdown gave some staff hours to do hundreds of reviews
Review of Contracts Terminated for Convenience (Report 25-03033-230)

status_summary: No department-wide audit modeled on the Defense Department audit was found. In February 2025 VA reviewed its contracts: on 2025-02-21 contracting offices were given less than 11 hours to review 1,049 contract actions, and on 2025-02-25 senior advisers and DOGE representatives directed terminations. A VA Inspector General report dated 2026-09-22, prepared at congressional request, found 435 of 2,210 reviewed contract actions, worth about $1.1 billion, had been terminated for convenience and that VA's lists of terminations sent to Congress were inaccurate. The report is a contract termination review rather than an audit of IT, management and finance, so it is recorded as a parallel step.

timeline.event: VA acquisition officials and a senior adviser gave contracting offices less than 11 hours to review 1,049 contract actions (per VA Inspector General report 25-03033-230).
VA senior advisers and DOGE representatives directed contract terminations although some offices had not finished their reviews (per VA Inspector General report 25-03033-230).

VA Inspector General issued report 25-03033-230, Review of Contracts Terminated for Convenience, finding 435 of 2,210 reviewed contract actions (about $1.1 billion) were terminated for convenience and that VA's lists of terminations sent to Congress were inaccurate; it made no recommendations.

title: Conduct an independent audit of VA to find IT, financial and contracting deficiencies
uncertainties: The Inspector General report 25-03033-230 was read on vaoig.gov in review on 2026-10-18 and by the researcher; it was conducted under inspection and evaluation standards at the request of two Senators and covers contract terminations and the accuracy of reported values, not IT, management or financial systems. The researcher noted that its executive summary and body differ on one count (1,775 versus 1,675 actions never terminated); the body figure is used. News coverage dated 2026-09-24 (Military Times, Government Executive) is kept as sources, and the news-dated event is replaced by the report's own date. VA's annual financial statement audit is routine and was not treated as the recommended audit. No search was made for a planned department-wide audit beyond earlier checks, so the stage also rests on the absence of one; the five systematic absence checks were not run.
